newsitem.title: POLAND: VW TO BOOST POLISH ASSEMBLY PLANT OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: VW TO BOOST POLISH ASSEMBLY PLANT OUTPUT.

text.p: Volkswagen AG will increase the number of cars it assembles in Poland by at least 50 percent to about 50,000 units in 1997, a senior official of the company's Polish unit said on Thursday.
"The production rise in 1997 will amount to between 50 and 75 percent depending on the market's demand," Adam Dobielinski, a member of Volkswagen-Poznan's management board, told Reuters.
He added that most of the output would be destined for the Polish market except for the Volkswagen Transport model, production of which would amount to 18,400 units.

He said Volkswagen's Polish plant, near the western city of Poznan, would assemble at least 25,000 models of the Skoda Felicia, 5,000 of the Seat Cordoba, 5,000 Polos and 500 Audi models. Assembly of the Skoda Octavia is being considered.

New car sales in Poland jumped 39.7 percent in the first 11 months of 1996 compared with the same period of 1995, showing Europe's biggest growth rate, according to independent monitoring agency Samar.
The report showed 347,845 new passenger cars were registered in January-October, compared with 248,947 in the same period of the previous year.
The robust car sales were fuelled by growth in real wages and expansion of credit by banks.
